clue.text: Not the same after start of business trouble

indicators.note: after places the phrase for 'not the same' behind the opening letter
start of picks the opening letter of the word business

parts.note: first letter of business
something not the same is other

explanation.surface: A firm runs into difficulty that is different from before, right as it starts up.
explanation.definitionFit: To bother someone is to trouble or disturb them; the two verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Before getting an opportunity perhaps

parts.note: by means before a given time, as in 'by Friday'
an opportunity is a chance

explanation.surface: Maybe someone will be given a break before long.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens by chance happens perhaps, through accident rather than design.

clue.text: Volunteers seizing reckless traitor in a restaurant

indicators.note: seizing means the volunteers' letters hold the rearranged word inside them

parts.note: the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve force

indicators.note: reckless suggests the letters of traitor are thrown around

explanation.surface: Volunteer soldiers arrest a careless traitor inside an eatery.
explanation.definitionFit: A trattoria is an informal Italian eating place serving simple food.

clue.text: Somewhat nominal exemption sent up with style

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means the hidden letters read from bottom to top
somewhat means only part of the words is used, a run of letters hidden within them

explanation.surface: A small tax exemption is mocked in a stylish way.
explanation.definitionFit: Elan is flair or dash, a stylish vigour in how something is done.

clue.text: Piece of info largely introduced to frighten Capone

indicators.note: introduced to means put inside the word for frighten

parts.note: to frighten is to scare

indicators.note: largely means most of the word, so its last letter is dropped

parts.note: a piece of information is a fact

explanation.surface: A snippet of information is used to scare the gangster Al Capone.
explanation.definitionFit: Scarface was the nickname of the Chicago gangster Al Capone, from scars on his cheek.

clue.text: The most essential part unfinished on delicate architectural feature

indicators.note: unfinished means the word for the central part loses its last letter

parts.note: the core is the central, most essential part
nice can mean delicate or subtle, as in a nice distinction

explanation.surface: The heart of the matter is left incomplete on a fragile piece of building design.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornice is a decorative moulding along the top of a wall or building.

clue.text: Study reportedly featuring fossil fuel lobby's ends again and again

indicators.note: featuring means the fuel word appears inside the sounded word
reportedly means the word for study is spoken, which is said like the waterside plant

parts.note: to study is to read, said like reed
peat is decayed vegetation burnt as fuel

indicators.note: ends takes the first and last letters of lobby

parts.note: the outside letters of lobby

explanation.surface: A report on the fossil fuel lobby is described as being repeated over and over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reportedly' applies only to Study: the spoken word for study is a homophone of the waterside plant, which then has the fuel set inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Repeatedly means many times over, so it means again and again.

clue.text: Set aside article on the beginnings of nationalisation under Labour

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: the beginnings of takes the first letter of each of the three words that follow

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece on the start of state ownership under a Labour government is overturned.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare invalid, as a court can set aside a marriage or a verdict.

clue.text: Concede after initially failing to crack cipher

indicators.note: to crack something is to break it up, so the remaining letters are rearranged
initially failing means the first letter of concede drops out

explanation.surface: Admit defeat after not managing at first to break a code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crack' and 'cipher' share a code-breaking surface, but 'crack' rearranges ONCEDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To cipher a message, as a verb, is to put it into code, to encode it.

clue.text: Mean to make money outside of Germany to support son

indicators.note: to support in a down clue means the following letters go below the son's letter

parts.note: tin is old British slang for money

indicators.note: outside of takes the first and last letters of Germany

parts.note: the outer letters of Germany

explanation.surface: Someone aims to earn cash abroad to keep their son.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to make' is link words; 'Mean' is the adjective, not 'intend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Stingy means ungenerous with money, which is what a mean person is.

clue.text: Case for a cymbal say

definitions.meaning: first meaning: an odd or eccentric person, as in 'he's a real case'
second meaning: a cymbal said aloud is a symbol

explanation.walkthrough: The second definition works by sound: 'say' turns cymbal into symbol, and a letter or sign is a character.
explanation.definitionFit: A character is both an eccentric person (a case) and a written sign or symbol.

clue.text: Good to include a note on opening of conventional flap

indicators.note: to include means the word for good holds the next letters inside it

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good
n. is the abbreviation for a note, as in a footnote reference

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of conventional

parts.note: first letter of conventional

explanation.surface: Instructions for a ballot: good people should add a note at the start of a conventional procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: A flap is a state of agitated alarm, so being in a flap is being in a panic.

clue.text: Retracted part of last cat book

indicators.note: Retracted says the hidden letters are read backwards
part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cat draws back its claws, as the last one in a story might.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts, the Acts of the Apostles, is a book of the New Testament.

clue.text: Letter about fellow consumed by absurd drivel is matchless

indicators.note: about means the Greek letter is turned round

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet

indicators.note: consumed by means the man's name goes inside the rearranged letters
absurd suggests the letters of drivel are made nonsense of and rearranged

parts.note: Al is a man's name, standing for any fellow

explanation.surface: A letter about some man is swallowed up by a load of absurd nonsense, which is unmatched.
explanation.walkthrough: The letter is Greek; 'fellow' is a stock crossword way of giving a short man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unrivalled has no equal or competitor, so it is matchless.

clue.text: Assemble to protect a right withdrawn in dispute

indicators.note: to protect means the assembling word surrounds the reversed letters

parts.note: to convene is to assemble

indicators.note: withdrawn means the letters for a right are drawn back, read in reverse

explanation.surface: People gather to defend a right that has been taken away in a disagreement.
explanation.definitionFit: To contravene a claim is to contradict or challenge it, a sense close to dispute.

clue.text: Hasty scoundrel regretful right away

parts.note: a cur is a contemptible man, a scoundrel

indicators.note: right away tells us the abbreviation for right is taken out

parts.note: regretful means sorry

explanation.surface: A rash villain says sorry immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'right away' looks like 'immediately', but it is the abbreviation R being removed from SORRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A cursory look is a hasty, superficial one, done without care.

clue.text: Become equal partners originally going after alternative venue

indicators.note: going after places the partner's initial behind the rearranged letters
an alternative version of venue is its letters rearranged
originally picks the first letter of partners

parts.note: first letter of partners

explanation.surface: Two partners draw level once they move on to a different venue.
explanation.definitionFit: To even up is to make or become level, balancing two sides so they are equal.

clue.text: In an excited state Rod describes most of them as slightly mad

indicators.note: describes means draws around, so the outer letters encircle the shortened word

parts.note: someone excited is up, keyed up
a pole is a rod

indicators.note: most of means the last letter of them is dropped

explanation.surface: An excited man called Rod depicts most of the people as a bit crazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name but is a pole; 'describes' is used in its geometric sense of drawing round.
explanation.definitionFit: Up the pole is British slang for crazy or eccentric, a little unhinged.

clue.text: Austrian nationalist's story is revealing

parts.note: William Tell, the legendary hero who led resistance to Austrian rule, is loosely called a nationalist here
a story is a tale

explanation.surface: A patriot's story tells all.
explanation.walkthrough: Tell is really the Swiss national hero who defied the Austrians; the clue's 'Austrian' points at that struggle.
explanation.definitionFit: A telltale sign gives something away, so it is revealing, as an adjective.

clue.text: Frequently repeated slogan of American conservationists taken in by Mr Agnew at first

indicators.note: taken in by means the conservation letters go inside the name's letters

parts.note: Mr taken as written, its letters MR
the NT, the National Trust, is a British conservation charity

indicators.note: at first picks the opening letter of Agnew

parts.note: first letter of Agnew

explanation.surface: A slogan of US environmentalists is adopted by a Mr Agnew, perhaps the US vice-president Spiro Agnew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at first' applies only to Agnew; Mr is kept whole. The National Trust is a British charity, so 'American' must supply its own letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantra is a word or phrase repeated often, originally a sacred chant used in meditation.

clue.text: An improbable account holding up heartless Alf as kindly

indicators.note: holding up in a down clue means the story sits beneath the shortened name, supporting it
heartless means the middle letter of Alf is removed

parts.note: a fable is a far-fetched story

explanation.surface: A tall tale props up poor Alf, who has lost heart, as a good-natured gesture.
explanation.definitionFit: Affable means friendly and good-natured, so an affable person behaves kindly.

clue.text: Grant found in bed with English novelist

indicators.note: found in means the word for grant is placed inside the word for bed

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
to let is to grant or allow

explanation.surface: Someone called Grant is discovered in bed with an English writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Grant' looks like a surname (Hugh Grant, perhaps) but is the verb meaning allow.
explanation.definitionFit: Colette was the pen name of the French author Sidonie-Gabrielle Colette, who wrote Gigi.

clue.text: Bob's short and extremely slimy

parts.note: curt means short, brusque

indicators.note: extremely takes the letters at the extremes of slimy, its first and last

explanation.surface: A man named Bob is brief and very creepy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a name but is the verb for a quick bending of the knees.
explanation.definitionFit: To bob is to make a quick bow or bend of the knee, which is what a curtsy is.

clue.text: Borrowed from John's oddly neglected single by the sound of it

indicators.note: oddly neglected means the odd-placed letters of John's are dropped, leaving the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of John's

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word for single is spoken, giving a homophone

parts.note: single means lone

explanation.surface: Taken from John, whose lonely record is ignored, it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on loan is lent for a time, so it is borrowed rather than owned.

clue.text: Deny the opportunity to debate normal pot use around France

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters sit round the letter for France
to use something here is to work it over, so the letters of normal pot are rearranged

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

explanation.surface: A debate about ordinary cannabis use is shut down in France.
explanation.definitionFit: To no-platform someone is to refuse them a venue to speak, denying them a chance to argue their case.

clue.text: Safe for fellow hiding in Togo's capital? Just the opposite

indicators.note: hiding in signals one piece concealed inside another
Just the opposite reverses the hiding, so the fellow word holds the capital letter

parts.note: a peer is a fellow or equal

indicators.note: capital is the first letter of Togo's

explanation.surface: Is a safe place for a man hiding in the capital of Togo? No, quite the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: Read literally, PEER would hide in T; 'Just the opposite' flips it so T hides in PEER. Peter is old criminal slang for a safe.
explanation.definitionFit: In underworld slang a peter is a safe or strongbox, and a peterman is a safe-breaker.

clue.text: Actually existing somewhere in Canada? Not half

indicators.note: Not half means one half of the place name is dropped and the second half kept

parts.note: Montreal is a city in Quebec, Canada

explanation.surface: Is a place in Canada genuinely there? Not by half.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not half' is also a British slang reply meaning 'very much so', adding to the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Something real truly exists rather than being imagined or fictional.

clue.text: Key entirely made of brass

parts.note: G is a musical key
all means entirely, as in all alone

explanation.surface: A key made wholly of the yellow metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brass' looks like the metal but means cheek or nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Brass and gall are both informal words for cheek or impudence.

clue.text: Outrageous when not in use against soldiers

indicators.note: against means the soldiers are placed next to the first part

parts.note: a light or fashion that is not in use is out
the RE, the Royal Engineers, is a British Army corps

explanation.surface: Something shocking when it is unused and turned against the troops.
explanation.definitionFit: Outre is a French loan word for something bizarre or unconventional, beyond what is proper.

clue.text: Answer accepted by outstanding star of dance

indicators.note: accepted by means the letter for answer is taken inside the combined words

parts.note: a boss is a raised knob, so it stands out
a nova is a star that suddenly brightens

explanation.surface: The response is welcomed by the leading performer of a dance show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outstanding' is literal: a boss is a projecting stud, as on a shield.
explanation.definitionFit: The bossa nova is a Brazilian style of music and the dance performed to it.

clue.text: Scandinavians finding sermon oddly in French

indicators.note: oddly means the letters of sermon are arranged in a strange order

parts.note: en is the French word for in

explanation.surface: Nordic people hear a sermon delivered strangely in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Norsemen were the people of medieval Scandinavia, the Vikings.

clue.text: Assert without proof of everyone say taking Ecstasy

indicators.note: taking means the drug's letter is added on at the end

parts.note: everyone is all
say means for example, abbreviated eg
E is the abbreviation for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A claim, unsupported, that everybody is taking ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: To allege is to claim something is true without yet proving it, as in an accusation.
